method: Direct review of six CatholicCulture-hosted DIRECTIONS reproducing Trapp (1955), Berger (1949) and Newland (1956); each described action anchored to line in hosted article. Not an original printed-book facsimile check; source-dependent recommendations not independent eyewitness attestations. Six further Newland hosted passages covered, including derivative Jesse-tree and home Tenebrae-inspired Stations; passage-level review does not verify original printed book or current prescribed indulgence.

source_groups.author: Maria Augusta Trapp
source_groups.book_source: Around the Year with the Trapp Family (1955)
source_groups.source_scope_caveat: Explicit eyewitness account of the Trapp family's Christmas Eve ceremony, with occasional wider claims; no universal ritual ownership inferred.

source_groups.author: Florence Berger
source_groups.source_scope_caveat: Mix of Berger family's Wisconsin reminiscence, parish blessing at High Mass, forgotten local custom in another parish, folk beliefs and author's household dishes; neither blessing nor superstitious efficacy universalized.

source_groups.author: Florence Berger
source_groups.source_scope_caveat: Berger reports Sicilian St Joseph table and poor beneficiaries; explicitly says her family did not stage so large an observance. Recipes are narrower author suggestions, not evidence of separate Catholic customs.

source_groups.author: Mary Reed Newland
source_groups.source_scope_caveat: Domestic Advent wreath: multiple construction, candle, prayer, teaching and family lighting variations described as practice or advice by one author, attached to already-published Advent wreath identity; no separate new customs.

source_groups.author: Mary Reed Newland
source_groups.source_scope_caveat: Newland suggests a private home vigil with texts reused from church liturgy and explicitly states some blessings are out of context; reserve church rite and lay devotional adaptation in separate lanes. No claim of authorized priestly blessing by lay leader.

source_groups.author: Mary Reed Newland
source_groups.source_scope_caveat: Domestic family Rogation walk and Litany personally adapted; priestly leading/blessing remains ministerial; French Canadian grains and monastery procession are distinct reported regional or institutional practices.

source_groups.author: Mary Reed Newland
source_groups.source_scope_caveat: Newland proposes daily sacrifices and household trackers; story of Juggler illustrative, not evidence of ritual practice; a cradle of good deeds relates to existing ADVT-002 but must not be collapsed into all possible sacrifice counters.

source_groups.author: Mary Reed Newland
source_groups.source_scope_caveat: German candle custom expressly named; author distinguishes original German mantle from her family's salvation-history illustrations. The candle is not automatically an officially blessed Paschal or Candlemas candle.

source_groups.author: Mary Reed Newland
source_groups.source_scope_caveat: Family craft models restored Easter Vigil Paschal candle with cloves replacing ritual incense inserts; do not claim a consecrated Paschal candle or permitted home liturgical ceremony.

source_groups.author: Mary Reed Newland
source_groups.source_scope_caveat: Author explicitly recalls an earlier Sister Margaret Rose article in Worship: derivative idea, not independent invention/attestation. Her family gives adaptations, tree prayer is domestic leader usage requiring authority review.

source_groups.author: Mary Reed Newland
source_groups.source_scope_caveat: Author lists alternative possible calendar designs; four rows are variants within one authored planning description, not four independently attested historical customs.

No indulgence attached on the basis of these pages alone.
